subject.title: [Bug] v2026.6.11 published dist missing reentrancy guard - reply session initialization conflicted

question: Should maintainers publish a stable hotfix/rebuilt package for the affected `2026.6.11` npm latest artifact, or leave this for the next stable train with an affected-version notice?
rationale: Current main is repaired, but npm latest stable remains affected; choosing a hotfix, stable replacement, or documented wait is a release-owner decision outside a source-only repair PR.

options.title: Publish Stable Hotfix
options.body: Rebuild and publish a stable package containing the current session writer and reply-init fixes, then validate the tarball chunks before closing.

options.title: Wait For Next Stable
options.body: Keep this open and clearly mark `2026.6.11` as affected until the next stable release replaces npm latest.

options.title: Redirect To Beta
options.body: Tell affected users to use the beta temporarily, but keep the stable-release issue open until npm latest is no longer affected.

recommendation.title: Publish Stable Hotfix
recommendation.body: Rebuild and publish a stable package containing the current session writer and reply-init fixes, then validate the tarball chunks before closing.

likelyOwner.reason: The remaining blocker is stable package release inclusion, and the latest stable release commit is attributed to Vincent Koc.
